No power specification is published, and available aggregator sources do not track small rural exchange facilities, so its current capacity is unknown. No colocation-grade data center specifications are documented.

Missouri has eight mapped data center facilities total, with no published power capacity from any operator spec pages this site has read. This campus cannot be ranked against other Missouri facilities by power because no megawatt figure exists for any of them in published specifications.

For AI infrastructure planning, this site does not factor into grid or scaling analysis. Rural telephone exchanges serve legacy voice and broadband networks rather than cloud computing or AI workloads, and the absence of published capacity figures confirms it is not marketed as a colocation resource.
